title: SOS! Save Our Seats Protest at Indiana Governor's Mansion
description:
Indivisible Central Indiana is announcing an emergency rally —“SOS: Save Our Seats”— to coincide with Vice President J.D. Vance’s visit to the Hoosier state on Thursday, August 7, 2025, from 4 - 6 pm at the Governor’s mansion. Vance’s closed-door meeting with Governor Mike Braun is likely aimed at securing a special legislative session to redraw Indiana’s congressional map and eliminate the state’s two Democratic seats. Indiana already tilts 7-to-2 for the GOP in Congress, and outside operatives want to eliminate the voice of the people. 

Mid-cycle redistricting is usually reserved for the history books, yet GOP strategists are reviving it from Texas to Indiana to lock in power before 2026 because they know their dangerous actions are so unpopular with a majority of Americans. As the Wall Street Journal noted, “Former President Donald Trump has catalyzed a nationwide scramble … by pushing a mid-decade redistricting effort in Texas, aiming to add five new Republican congressional seats.” The Brennan Center warns that existing gerrymanders already “give Republicans an advantage of around 16 House seats” even under today’s maps—an edge that could grow if more states follow Texas’s lead. 

Vice-President J.D. Vance’s trip to Indianapolis is part of that playbook; Governor Mike Braun conceded that national operatives are “going to come into every state that’s got the possibility of that happening,” with Indiana’s lone competitive district in the crosshairs. Voting-rights advocates say the push echoes the 2003 Texas power grab later struck down in court and amounts to an “extraordinary power grab” that would silence diverse communities, erode public trust, and reshape Congress for the rest of the decade.

Indivisible Central Indiana encourages Hoosiers to join us outside of the Governor’s Mansion to peacefully protest this clear power grab to take away voters’ voices. 

When: Thursday, August 7, 2025
Time: 4-6 p.m. ET
Location: Governor’s Mansion, 4750 N Meridian St, Indianapolis, IN 46208

title: Panel: Run for Climate
description:
**What if thousands of us ran for local office on climate?** With climate action stalled federally, cities, counties, and states have a huge opportunity to lead, which is why we need progressive climate champions in office at all levels of government now more than ever.

**On August 27 at 6pm ET/3pm PT, Lead Locally is hosting a virtual panel featuring elected climate leaders from across the country.** In this moment, voters are calling for a change in leadership – generationally, and politically – at all levels of government. 

Zohran Mamdani’s historic win in NYC’s mayoral primary, for instance, provides one exciting model of what new leadership on climate can look like. From fare-free buses to green public schools, his bold climate platform centered on making the city more affordable and livable for working class families.

**Panelists will share with us:**

* How they successfully ran for local office – and what motivated them to do so

* How they’re governing in the face of Trump’s attacks on our planet and communities

* Whether, and in what way, they think voters are demanding a change in leadership right now – and what races like Mamdani’s can tell us 

This call is for all, whether you are just curious about local climate politics or you are committed to running for local office already.

_Lead Locally is building local power to stop fossil fuels and build a just, green economy from the grassroots up. Learn more: https://leadlocally.org/._

re Board of Supervisors:

The County Board of Supervisors are elected to four-year terms and provide direction to the County Administrator and several other county departments.

The board is like the City Council, except its jurisdiction covers all the county and unincorporated areas.

Board members decide the county tax rate and approve the county budget.

The County Board of Supervisors oversees health, road, parks, libraries, law enforcement, and other municipal services. The Board also has the power to fill vacancies in the county and legislative offices, other boards and commissions, pass resolutions, and enact ordinances and regulations as authorized by state law.

The Board has the authority to make decisions on a variety of issues, such as zoning changes, resolutions, and ordinances.

Additionally, the board of supervisors has the power to remove and replace election precincts, appoint election inspectors and judges as well as canvass election returns, declare election results, and issue certificates.
